- **Proposals**: Research proposal and project application forms
- **Ethics**: Ethics review and compliance forms
- **Lab Management**: Laboratory access and equipment request forms
- **Data**: Data access and management forms
- **Funding**: Grant application templates and funding forms
- **Collaboration**: Collaboration agreement templates
- **Publications**: Publication submission and documentation forms

## Submission Instructions

Completed forms should be submitted to:
- **Email**: surc@su.edu.krd
- **Subject**: Form Name - [Your Name]
- **Processing Time**: 3-5 business days for standard forms

For urgent requests, please contact the relevant department directly.

## Research Ethics

All research conducted under SURC must adhere to the highest ethical standards. Our ethics guidelines cover:

- Informed consent procedures
- Protection of human subjects
- Animal research ethics
- Data privacy and confidentiality
- Conflict of interest management
- Ethical review processes

## Data Management

Research data management is crucial for research integrity and reproducibility. Our policies ensure:

- Proper data documentation and metadata
- Secure data storage and backup procedures
- Data sharing and open access principles
- Data retention and archiving policies
- Compliance with data protection regulations

## Compliance and Review

All research projects must undergo appropriate ethical review and comply with:

- University research policies
- National research regulations
- International research standards
- Funding agency requirements
- Institutional review board guidelines

For questions about regulations and guidelines, please contact the Research Ethics Committee at ethics@su.edu.krd.

service_item.content: The Salahaddin University Research Center (SURC) is guided by a dedicated board that provides strategic direction, ensures alignment with the university’s mission, and safeguards the quality and ethics of all research activities. The board brings together experienced academics and institutional leaders who oversee priority setting, evaluation of major projects, and the development of long-term partnerships. Working alongside them is a diverse community of researchers—from senior professors to early-career scholars and graduate students—who lead interdisciplinary projects across biology, environmental studies, social sciences, data analysis, and other fields. Together, the board and researchers form a collaborative ecosystem that combines strategic vision with hands-on scientific work, turning ideas into impactful research outcomes for the university and the wider community.

frontmatter.title: Data Science Workshop: Advanced Analytics Techniques
frontmatter.description: Hands-on workshop on advanced data analytics and machine learning applications.

events.body:
This intensive workshop will cover advanced data science techniques including machine learning, statistical modeling, and data visualization. Participants will work with real datasets and learn practical applications.

## Workshop Topics

- Machine learning algorithms
- Statistical analysis methods
- Data visualization best practices
- Python and R programming

## Prerequisites

Basic knowledge of statistics and programming recommended.

frontmatter.title: Molecular Biology Research Seminar Series
frontmatter.description: Monthly seminar series featuring cutting-edge research in molecular biology and genetics.

events.body:
Our monthly research seminar series continues with presentations on the latest advances in molecular biology, genetics, and biotechnology. Graduate students and researchers will share their findings.

## This Month's Presentations

- Gene expression analysis in plant systems
- CRISPR technology applications
- Protein structure and function studies
- Bioinformatics tools and resources

## Open to All

Students, faculty, and researchers are welcome to attend.

frontmatter.title: Environmental Monitoring Field Trip
frontmatter.description: Field trip to environmental monitoring sites to observe data collection methods.

events.body:
Join our environmental research team for a hands-on field trip to various monitoring sites. Learn about air quality, water quality, and soil sampling techniques used in environmental research.

## Activities

- Site visits to monitoring stations
- Hands-on sampling demonstrations
- Data collection techniques
- Equipment operation training

## Requirements

Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing required. Transportation provided.

frontmatter.title: Chemistry Lab Safety Training Session
frontmatter.description: Comprehensive safety training for all chemistry laboratory users.

events.body:
Mandatory safety training session for all students and researchers using chemistry laboratories. This session covers safety protocols, emergency procedures, and proper handling of chemicals.

## Topics Covered

- Laboratory safety protocols
- Chemical handling and storage
- Emergency response procedures
- Personal protective equipment
- Waste disposal guidelines

## Certification

Completion certificate will be provided upon successful completion of the training.

frontmatter.title: Social Sciences Research Methodology Workshop
frontmatter.description: Workshop on research methodologies for social sciences and humanities.

events.body:
This workshop provides comprehensive training on research methodologies used in social sciences, including survey design, qualitative research methods, and data analysis techniques.

## Workshop Content

- Survey design and implementation
- Interview techniques
- Focus group facilitation
- Qualitative data analysis
- Ethical considerations in social research

## Target Audience

Graduate students and early-career researchers in social sciences and humanities.

frontmatter.title: Agricultural Research Open Day
frontmatter.description: Open day showcasing agricultural research projects and innovations.

events.body:
Visit our agricultural research station to see ongoing projects, meet researchers, and learn about innovations in sustainable farming practices. This event is open to the public.

## Activities

- Research project demonstrations
- Farm tours
- Interactive exhibits
- Q&A sessions with researchers
- Seed and plant distribution

## Family Friendly

All ages welcome. Refreshments provided.

frontmatter.title: Materials Science Conference: Innovations in Industrial Applications
frontmatter.description: Two-day conference on materials science and its industrial applications.

events.body:
Join us for a comprehensive conference on the latest developments in materials science, featuring presentations from leading researchers and industry professionals.

## Conference Themes

- Advanced materials synthesis
- Nanotechnology applications
- Industrial materials processing
- Sustainable materials development
- Materials characterization techniques

## Registration

Early bird registration available until April 25, 2024.

frontmatter.title: Student Research Poster Competition
frontmatter.description: Annual competition showcasing undergraduate and graduate student research projects.

events.body:
Students from all disciplines are invited to present their research projects in poster format. This competition recognizes outstanding student research and provides networking opportunities.

## Competition Categories

- Undergraduate Research
- Master's Thesis Projects
- Doctoral Research
- Interdisciplinary Projects

## Prizes

Cash prizes and certificates will be awarded to winners in each category.

## Registration Deadline

May 1, 2024

frontmatter.title: Research Ethics and Integrity Training
frontmatter.description: Training session on research ethics, integrity, and responsible conduct of research.

events.body:
Essential training for all researchers on ethical conduct in research, including topics on data integrity, authorship, conflict of interest, and research misconduct.

## Training Modules

- Research ethics principles
- Data management and integrity
- Authorship and publication ethics
- Conflict of interest management
- Research misconduct prevention

## Certification

This training is required for all researchers and provides certification upon completion.

frontmatter.title: Adolescents' Social Phobia and its relationship to Parental treatment methods: A field study in Erbil city center
frontmatter.description: Using scales validated through Cronbach's alpha, researchers surveyed 402 high‑school students in Erbil to assess social phobia prevalence and parental treatment methods. Analysis showed teenagers had very low levels of social phobia; parents predominantly used democratic parenting, and no significant differences were found by gender, grade level or school type.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This field study examined the relationship between parental treatment methods and social phobia prevalence among adolescents in Erbil city center. The research surveyed 402 high‑school students using validated psychological assessment scales to evaluate social anxiety levels and parental disciplinary approaches.

## Methodology

The study employed standardized scales validated through Cronbach's alpha for reliability assessment. A total of 402 high‑school students from various schools in Erbil city center participated in the survey. Data collection focused on social phobia symptoms and parental treatment methods.

## Key Findings

The research revealed several important findings:

- **Social Phobia Prevalence**: Teenagers in Erbil demonstrated very low levels of social phobia
- **Parenting Styles**: Parents predominantly used democratic parenting approaches
- **Demographic Factors**: No significant differences were found by gender, grade level, or school type
- **Parent-Child Relationship**: Democratic parenting was associated with lower social anxiety levels

## Implications

These findings have implications for:

- Mental health intervention strategies for adolescents
- Parent education programs focusing on effective parenting methods
- Understanding cultural factors in adolescent mental health

## Conclusion

The study highlights the positive association between democratic parenting and low social phobia levels in adolescents, providing valuable insights for mental health practitioners and families in the Kurdistan region.

frontmatter.title: Temporal patterns of cancer burden in Asia, 1990-2019
frontmatter.description: A systematic examination for the Global Burden of Disease study, analyzing cancer incidence and mortality trends across Asian demographics.

publications.body:
## Overview

This systematic examination for the Global Burden of Disease study provides a comprehensive analysis of cancer incidence and mortality trends across Asian demographics from 1990 to 2019. The research offers critical insights into the evolving patterns of cancer burden in Asia, identifying key epidemiological trends and regional variations.

## Key Findings

The study reveals significant temporal patterns in cancer burden across different Asian populations, highlighting:

- **Incidence Trends**: Detailed analysis of cancer incidence rates across various Asian demographic groups
- **Mortality Patterns**: Examination of cancer-related mortality trends and their contributing factors
- **Regional Variations**: Identification of geographical and demographic disparities in cancer burden
- **Temporal Changes**: Analysis of how cancer patterns have evolved over the three-decade study period

## Methodology

This research employed systematic data collection and analysis methods consistent with the Global Burden of Disease study framework, ensuring robust and comparable findings across diverse Asian populations.

## Implications

The findings contribute to our understanding of cancer epidemiology in Asia and inform public health policies and interventions aimed at reducing cancer burden across the region.

## Related Resources

For detailed data, methodology, and comprehensive findings, please refer to the full report available in PDF format.

frontmatter.title: Health problems of chemical bombardment survivors in Kurdistan
frontmatter.description: Comprehensive assessment of the long-term genetic and physiological health impacts on survivors of chemical weapon attacks.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This comprehensive report documents the long-term genetic and physiological health impacts on survivors of chemical weapon attacks in Kurdistan. The study provides detailed assessment of health consequences and identifies ongoing medical needs of affected populations.

## Methodology

The research employed comprehensive medical and genetic assessments of chemical bombardment survivors. Clinical examinations, genetic analysis, and epidemiological surveys were conducted to evaluate both immediate and long-term health effects.

## Key Findings

The study revealed significant health impacts:

- **Long-Term Health Effects**: Persistent genetic and physiological consequences of chemical exposure
- **Genetic Alterations**: Identification of genetic changes associated with chemical exposure
- **Physiological Impacts**: Chronic health conditions affecting survivors
- **Medical Needs**: Ongoing healthcare requirements for affected populations

## Implications

These findings have important implications for:

- Medical care and treatment of survivors
- Public health policies addressing chemical warfare impacts
- Understanding long-term consequences of chemical exposure

## Conclusion

The report highlights the devastating and persistent health impacts of chemical bombardment on survivors in Kurdistan, emphasizing the need for continued medical support and research into effective treatments for chemical exposure-related conditions.

frontmatter.title: Assessment the Clean Index and Fertilizing Index of Some Imported Composts to Erbil City
frontmatter.description: Researchers evaluated composts from various countries imported to Erbil using a completely randomized design. Fertilizer index values ranged from 4.13 to 4.47 and clean index values from 3.20 to 3.93, indicating medium heavy‑metal content; overall the composts had good quality suitable for agricultural land.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This study evaluated the quality and safety of imported composts available in Erbil city, assessing both their fertilizing potential and heavy metal content. The research examined composts from various countries to determine their suitability for agricultural use in the Kurdistan region.

## Methodology

The study employed a completely randomized design to evaluate composts imported from different countries. Quality assessments included analysis of fertilizer indices and clean indices, measuring nutrient content and heavy metal contamination levels.

## Key Findings

The research revealed important quality indicators:

- **Fertilizer Index**: Values ranged from 4.13 to 4.47, indicating good nutrient content
- **Clean Index**: Values ranged from 3.20 to 3.93, suggesting medium heavy‑metal content
- **Overall Quality**: The composts demonstrated good quality suitable for agricultural land use
- **Heavy Metal Assessment**: Medium levels of heavy metals were detected, within acceptable agricultural limits

## Implications

These findings have practical applications for:

- Agricultural producers selecting compost materials
- Ensuring soil health and crop safety
- Environmental management and sustainable agriculture practices

## Conclusion

The study confirms that imported composts in Erbil meet quality standards for agricultural use, providing valuable information for farmers and agricultural professionals in the region while highlighting the importance of regular quality monitoring.

frontmatter.title: Assessing air quality impacts of gas stations through heavy metal analysis
frontmatter.description: Occupational health study utilizing scalp hair and dust analysis to measure heavy metal exposure in gas station employees.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This occupational health study assessed air quality impacts and heavy metal exposure among gas station employees using biomonitoring techniques. The research utilized scalp hair and dust analysis to measure occupational exposure levels and assess health risks.

## Methodology

The study employed biomonitoring methods including scalp hair analysis and workplace dust sampling to assess heavy metal exposure. Gas station employees were evaluated for exposure levels, and environmental samples were analyzed for heavy metal contamination.

## Key Findings

The research revealed important findings:

- **Exposure Assessment**: Quantification of heavy metal exposure levels in gas station workers
- **Biomonitoring Data**: Heavy metal concentrations measured in scalp hair and workplace dust
- **Occupational Risks**: Identification of health risks associated with workplace exposure
- **Environmental Impact**: Assessment of air quality impacts from gas station operations

## Implications

These findings have important applications for:

- Occupational health and safety regulations
- Worker protection programs and exposure monitoring
- Environmental health standards in the petroleum retail industry

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates measurable heavy metal exposure in gas station employees, highlighting the importance of workplace safety measures and regular biomonitoring to protect worker health and ensure air quality standards.

frontmatter.title: Hematological Alterations Linked to Occupational Heavy Metal Exposure in Gasoline Station Workers: A Biomonitoring Study From Erbil City
frontmatter.description: A cross‑sectional biomonitoring study examined 75 gasoline‑station workers and 25 controls in Erbil, assessing blood counts and heavy‑metal concentrations. Exposed workers showed decreased haemoglobin and haematocrit, increased red and white blood cell counts, and higher lymphocyte percentages; heavy‑metal levels in scalp hair and dust correlated with these hematological changes.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This cross-sectional biomonitoring study investigated the health effects of occupational heavy metal exposure among gasoline station workers in Erbil city. The research assessed hematological parameters and heavy metal concentrations in exposed workers compared to controls.

## Methodology

The study examined 75 gasoline station workers and 25 control subjects in Erbil. Blood samples were analyzed for complete blood counts, while heavy metal concentrations were measured in scalp hair and workplace dust samples. Statistical analysis was performed to identify correlations between exposure and health effects.

## Key Findings

The research revealed significant health impacts:

- **Hematological Changes**: Exposed workers showed decreased hemoglobin and hematocrit levels
- **Blood Cell Alterations**: Increased red and white blood cell counts were observed
- **Lymphocyte Changes**: Higher lymphocyte percentages in exposed workers
- **Exposure Biomarkers**: Heavy metal levels in scalp hair and dust correlated with hematological alterations
- **Occupational Risk**: Workers demonstrated measurable health effects from occupational exposure

## Implications

These findings have important implications for:

- Occupational health and safety regulations
- Worker protection programs and medical monitoring
- Environmental health standards in the petroleum industry

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates significant hematological alterations in gasoline station workers exposed to heavy metals, emphasizing the need for improved occupational health protection measures and regular biomonitoring to safeguard worker health.

frontmatter.title: Structure of Description in the novel 'Hotel Europe' by Farhad Pirbal
frontmatter.description: Literary analysis of postmodern narrative techniques and descriptive structures in contemporary Kurdish fiction.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This literary analysis examines the structure of description in Farhad Pirbal's novel "Hotel Europe," focusing on postmodern narrative techniques and descriptive structures in contemporary Kurdish fiction. The study explores how descriptive elements contribute to meaning and narrative complexity in the work.

## Methodology

The research employed literary analysis methods to examine narrative structure, descriptive techniques, and postmodern elements in the novel. Close reading and theoretical analysis were used to interpret descriptive strategies and their functions.

## Key Findings

The analysis revealed significant insights:

- **Descriptive Structures**: Examination of how descriptive passages are organized and function within the narrative
- **Postmodern Techniques**: Identification of postmodern narrative strategies in Kurdish fiction
- **Narrative Innovation**: Analysis of innovative approaches to description and storytelling
- **Cultural Context**: Understanding of how description reflects cultural and social themes

## Implications

These findings contribute to:

- Understanding contemporary Kurdish literature
- Analysis of postmodern narrative techniques in regional fiction
- Literary criticism and theoretical approaches to descriptive writing

## Conclusion

The study provides valuable insights into the structure and function of description in contemporary Kurdish fiction, demonstrating how narrative techniques contribute to literary meaning and cultural expression in Farhad Pirbal's work.

frontmatter.title: Impact of IL‑6‑174G/C, IL‑10‑1082A/G Gene Polymorphisms on Toxoplasma gondii infections
frontmatter.description: This study assessed cytokine gene polymorphisms in 40 women with toxoplasmosis and 30 healthy controls. It found that specific IL‑6 and IL‑10 genotypes were associated with increased or decreased risk of Toxoplasma gondii infection; for example, the IL‑6‑174 CC genotype tripled infection risk while the IL‑10‑1082 mutant heterozygote showed a protective effect.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This study investigated the relationship between cytokine gene polymorphisms and susceptibility to *Toxoplasma gondii* infection. The research assessed IL‑6‑174G/C and IL‑10‑1082A/G polymorphisms in 40 women with confirmed toxoplasmosis and 30 healthy controls to determine genetic factors influencing infection risk.

## Methodology

Genetic analysis was performed on blood samples from 40 women diagnosed with toxoplasmosis and 30 healthy control subjects. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and genotyping techniques were employed to identify specific polymorphisms in the IL‑6 and IL‑10 cytokine genes.

## Key Findings

The study revealed significant associations between cytokine polymorphisms and infection susceptibility:

- **IL‑6‑174 CC Genotype**: Tripled the risk of *Toxoplasma gondii* infection compared to other genotypes
- **IL‑10‑1082 Mutant Heterozygote**: Demonstrated a protective effect against infection
- **Genetic Susceptibility**: Specific cytokine gene variants were associated with differential infection risk
- **Clinical Implications**: Genetic screening may help identify individuals at higher risk of toxoplasmosis

## Implications

These findings contribute to understanding the genetic basis of susceptibility to *Toxoplasma gondii* infection and may inform:

- Risk assessment strategies for high-risk populations
- Development of targeted prevention approaches
- Understanding individual differences in immune response to parasitic infections

## Conclusion

The study highlights the important role of cytokine gene polymorphisms in determining susceptibility to toxoplasmosis, providing valuable insights for both clinical practice and public health interventions.

frontmatter.title: LXR Inhibits Proliferation of Human Breast Cancer Cells through the PI3K‑Akt Pathway
frontmatter.description: This research demonstrates that activation of liver X receptors (LXRs) reduces proliferation of human breast cancer cells. LXRs inhibit PI3K‑Akt pathway signalling, increasing expression of phosphatases (PTEN, PHLPP, PHLPPL) and reducing phosphorylation of Akt and PI3K. The findings highlight LXRs as potential targets for cancer therapy.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This research demonstrates that activation of liver X receptors (LXRs) effectively reduces proliferation of human breast cancer cells through modulation of the PI3K‑Akt signaling pathway. The study provides mechanistic insights into how LXR activation can inhibit cancer cell growth and highlights potential therapeutic applications.

## Methodology

The study employed cell culture models of human breast cancer, treating cells with LXR agonists and analyzing cellular proliferation, pathway activation, and expression of key regulatory proteins. Western blotting and molecular biology techniques were used to assess signaling pathway components.

## Key Findings

The research revealed significant mechanistic insights:

- **Anti-Proliferative Effect**: LXR activation reduces breast cancer cell proliferation
- **Pathway Inhibition**: LXRs inhibit PI3K‑Akt pathway signaling activity
- **Phosphatase Induction**: Increased expression of tumor suppressor phosphatases (PTEN, PHLPP, PHLPPL)
- **Kinase Modulation**: Reduced phosphorylation of Akt and PI3K following LXR activation
- **Therapeutic Potential**: LXRs represent promising targets for breast cancer therapy

## Implications

These findings have important implications for:

- Development of novel therapeutic strategies for breast cancer treatment
- Understanding molecular mechanisms of cancer cell growth regulation
- Identification of new drug targets in the PI3K‑Akt pathway

## Conclusion

The study establishes LXRs as important regulators of breast cancer cell proliferation through PI3K‑Akt pathway modulation, providing a foundation for future therapeutic development targeting these nuclear receptors in cancer treatment.

frontmatter.title: Multi‑Factor Classification Using Deep Learning for X‑ray Images
frontmatter.description: This journal article proposes a deep‑learning model that performs multi‑factor classification on X‑ray images, enabling simultaneous diagnosis of multiple conditions. The approach improves diagnostic accuracy and efficiency by leveraging deep neural networks.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This research proposes an advanced deep learning architecture for multi-factor classification of X-ray images, enabling simultaneous diagnosis of multiple medical conditions from a single radiographic image. The approach leverages convolutional neural networks to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in medical imaging.

## Methodology

The study developed and trained deep neural network models using large datasets of X-ray images. The architecture was designed to perform multi-label classification, identifying multiple conditions simultaneously. Performance was evaluated using standard metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores.

## Key Findings

The research demonstrated significant improvements:

- **Multi-Factor Diagnosis**: The model successfully identifies multiple conditions from a single X-ray image
- **Diagnostic Accuracy**: Improved accuracy compared to traditional single-factor classification approaches
- **Efficiency**: Reduced processing time and computational requirements
- **Clinical Applications**: Practical implementation in medical diagnostic workflows

## Implications

These findings have important applications for:

- Medical imaging and diagnostic radiology
- Development of computer-aided diagnosis systems
- Improving healthcare delivery efficiency

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates the potential of deep learning for multi-factor classification in medical imaging, offering a promising approach to enhance diagnostic capabilities and improve patient care through advanced artificial intelligence techniques.

frontmatter.title: Monthly occurrence, maturation time and some host factor effects on the spirurine nematode Rhabdochona longispicula
frontmatter.description: The study collected Cyprinion macrostomus fish monthly from three points on the Greater Zab River in 2022 to determine infection prevalence and maturation of the nematode Rhabdochona longispicula. Results showed peak infection in May–June with prevalence up to 42.85 %, while host sex had no significant effect on infection but older fish had higher prevalence.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This study investigated the monthly occurrence and maturation time of the spirurine nematode *Rhabdochona longispicula* in *Cyprinion macrostomus* fish populations along the Greater Zab River. The research collected fish samples monthly from three strategic points during 2022 to determine infection prevalence and analyze host factors affecting parasitism.

## Methodology

Monthly sampling was conducted from three distinct locations along the Greater Zab River throughout 2022. Fish specimens were examined for nematode infections, with detailed analysis of parasite maturation stages and prevalence rates.

## Key Findings

The study revealed several important findings:

- **Seasonal Patterns**: Peak infection prevalence occurred during May–June, reaching up to 42.85%
- **Host Sex**: No significant correlation was found between host sex and infection prevalence
- **Age Factor**: Older fish demonstrated higher prevalence rates, suggesting age-related susceptibility
- **Maturation Dynamics**: The research provided insights into the maturation timeline of *Rhabdochona longispicula* within its host

## Implications

These findings contribute to understanding the epidemiology of fish parasites in the Greater Zab River ecosystem and may inform fisheries management and disease control strategies for native fish populations.

## Conclusion

The temporal and host factor analysis provides valuable information for managing parasitic infections in freshwater fish populations, with particular relevance for local fisheries and aquatic ecosystem health.

frontmatter.title: Nanoscale Zero‑Valent Iron Efficient for Remediation of Chromium, Nickel, and Cadmium‑Contaminated Soils Near Oil Refinery Sites
frontmatter.description: This study analyzed soils near an oil refinery in Erbil contaminated with heavy metals and tested remediation using green nanoscale zero‑valent iron (nZVI) nanoparticles. Soil samples showed elevated chromium (52.85–79.54 mg·kg⁻¹), nickel (41.10–63.42 mg·kg⁻¹) and cadmium (1.41–1.76 mg·kg⁻¹) exceeding baseline standards. Green nZVI, synthesized from lemon‑peel extract, achieved 12 %, 5 % and 6 % removal of Cr, Ni and Cd, respectively, offering a sustainable remediation approach.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This research investigated the use of green-synthesized nanoscale zero‑valent iron (nZVI) nanoparticles for remediating heavy metal-contaminated soils near oil refinery sites in Erbil. The study evaluated the effectiveness of environmentally friendly nZVI synthesized from lemon peel extract in removing chromium, nickel, and cadmium from contaminated soils.

## Methodology

Soil samples were collected from areas near an oil refinery in Erbil and analyzed for heavy metal contamination. Green nZVI nanoparticles were synthesized using lemon peel extract as a reducing agent. Remediation experiments were conducted to assess the efficiency of heavy metal removal.

## Key Findings

The study revealed significant contamination and remediation results:

- **Soil Contamination**: Elevated levels of chromium (52.85–79.54 mg·kg⁻¹), nickel (41.10–63.42 mg·kg⁻¹), and cadmium (1.41–1.76 mg·kg⁻¹) exceeding baseline standards
- **Remediation Efficiency**: Green nZVI achieved 12% removal of chromium, 5% removal of nickel, and 6% removal of cadmium
- **Sustainable Approach**: Lemon peel-synthesized nZVI offers an environmentally friendly remediation method
- **Practical Applications**: Demonstrates potential for field-scale soil remediation

## Implications

These findings have important applications for:

- Remediation of industrial contamination sites
- Development of sustainable nanotechnology solutions for environmental cleanup
- Protection of soil and water resources in industrial areas

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates the potential of green-synthesized nZVI nanoparticles for heavy metal remediation, providing a sustainable approach to addressing soil contamination near industrial facilities in the Kurdistan region.

frontmatter.title: Assessment of heavy metals in rainfall as an indicator of air pollution from Erbil Steel Factory in Iraq
frontmatter.description: This study measured heavy‑metal concentrations in rainfall near the Erbil Steel Factory, finding levels of Mn, Pb, Fe, As, Co, Se, Hg and Cd significantly higher than those at a rural control site. The geo‑accumulation index for Mn (6.28) indicated extreme contamination, and the pollution load index (13.46) showed the area is heavily metal‑polluted.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This environmental monitoring study assessed heavy metal contamination in rainfall near the Erbil Steel Factory, using atmospheric deposition as an indicator of air pollution. The research compared heavy metal concentrations between the industrial site and a rural control area to evaluate environmental impact.

## Methodology

Rainwater samples were collected from sites near the Erbil Steel Factory and compared with samples from a rural control location. Heavy metal analysis was performed for Mn, Pb, Fe, As, Co, Se, Hg, and Cd. Geo-accumulation index and pollution load index were calculated to assess contamination levels.

## Key Findings

The study revealed significant contamination:

- **Heavy Metal Levels**: Concentrations of Mn, Pb, Fe, As, Co, Se, Hg, and Cd were significantly higher near the factory compared to control sites
- **Geo-accumulation Index**: Mn showed an index of 6.28, indicating extreme contamination
- **Pollution Load Index**: The overall pollution load index of 13.46 demonstrates heavy metal pollution in the area
- **Environmental Impact**: Atmospheric deposition contributes significantly to environmental contamination

## Implications

These findings have important implications for:

- Environmental monitoring and pollution control strategies
- Public health protection in industrial areas
- Industrial emissions management and regulation

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates significant heavy metal contamination in rainfall near the Erbil Steel Factory, highlighting the need for improved air pollution control measures and continued environmental monitoring to protect public health and ecosystem integrity.

frontmatter.title: A Review of Criteria in Rain Water Harvesting Management
frontmatter.description: Published in the International Journal of Engineering and Natural Sciences, this article reviews key criteria for selecting suitable rainwater harvesting sites. It highlights the importance of remote sensing and GIS techniques and summarizes parameters used to optimize rainwater harvesting in arid regions.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This comprehensive review examines key criteria and methodologies for selecting suitable sites for rainwater harvesting systems, with particular emphasis on applications in arid and semi-arid regions. The article synthesizes findings from multiple studies to provide a framework for optimal site selection and system design.

## Methodology

The review analyzed peer-reviewed literature and case studies on rainwater harvesting site selection criteria. The research evaluated various parameters including climate, soil characteristics, topography, land use, and accessibility, synthesizing best practices from the field.

## Key Findings

The review identified critical factors for site selection:

- **Site Selection Criteria**: Key parameters include climate patterns, soil type, topography, and land use
- **Remote Sensing and GIS**: Geographic information systems and remote sensing techniques are essential for optimal site identification
- **Arid Region Optimization**: Specific considerations for maximizing water collection in water-scarce environments
- **Best Practices**: Evidence-based recommendations for system design and implementation

## Implications

These findings have practical applications for:

- Water resource management in arid regions
- Sustainable development and agricultural planning
- Climate change adaptation strategies

## Conclusion

The review provides valuable guidance for rainwater harvesting system planning and implementation, emphasizing the importance of integrated approaches combining geographic analysis, environmental assessment, and engineering design for optimal water resource management.

frontmatter.title: Genetic and non-genetic factors affecting in Saanen goat milk production
frontmatter.description: Quantitative analysis of heritability and environmental factors influencing the productive traits of Saanen goats in the Kurdistan Region.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This quantitative study analyzed genetic and non-genetic factors affecting milk production in Saanen goats in the Kurdistan Region. The research examined heritability estimates and environmental influences on productive traits, providing insights for breeding and management strategies.

## Methodology

The study employed quantitative genetic analysis to evaluate heritability estimates and environmental factors. Performance data from Saanen goats in the Kurdistan Region were analyzed using statistical models to separate genetic and environmental effects.

## Key Findings

The research revealed significant findings:

- **Heritability Estimates**: Quantitative analysis of genetic contributions to milk production traits
- **Environmental Factors**: Identification of non-genetic factors affecting productive performance
- **Trait Correlations**: Relationships between different productive traits in Saanen goats
- **Breeding Implications**: Practical applications for selection and breeding programs

## Implications

These findings have practical applications for:

- Breeding programs targeting improved milk production
- Management strategies optimizing environmental conditions
- Genetic improvement in Saanen goat populations

## Conclusion

The study provides valuable insights into genetic and environmental factors affecting milk production in Saanen goats, offering practical guidance for livestock improvement programs in the Kurdistan Region.

frontmatter.title: Genome Analysis of SARS‑CoV‑2 Delta variant in the Kurdistan region of Iraq
frontmatter.description: This genomic study sequenced SARS‑CoV‑2 Delta variant samples from West Erbil Emergency Hospital. The variant belonged to lineage B.1.617.2 and contained 13 mutations on the spike protein, including unique substitutions (E156G, T250I, T19A and L861W) not previously reported in Delta isolates. The findings underscore the need for further investigation of novel mutations and vaccine efficacy.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This comprehensive genomic study sequenced SARS‑CoV‑2 Delta variant samples collected from West Erbil Emergency Hospital in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. The research identified the variant as belonging to lineage B.1.617.2 and characterized multiple spike protein mutations, including several unique substitutions not previously documented in Delta isolates.

## Methodology

Whole genome sequencing was performed on SARS‑CoV‑2 samples from confirmed Delta variant cases. Advanced bioinformatics tools were employed to analyze mutations, identify lineage classification, and compare findings with global genomic databases.

## Key Findings

The genomic analysis revealed significant insights:

- **Lineage Classification**: Confirmed as B.1.617.2 Delta variant lineage
- **Spike Protein Mutations**: Identified 13 distinct mutations on the spike protein
- **Unique Substitutions**: Discovered four novel mutations (E156G, T250I, T19A, and L861W) not previously reported in Delta isolates
- **Regional Characteristics**: The Kurdistan region samples showed specific mutational patterns that may have implications for transmission and pathogenicity

## Implications

These findings highlight the importance of regional genomic surveillance in tracking SARS‑CoV‑2 evolution. The identification of unique mutations underscores the need for:

- Continued monitoring of viral evolution in the region
- Assessment of vaccine efficacy against region-specific variants
- Understanding potential impacts on diagnostic and therapeutic approaches

## Conclusion

This study contributes valuable genomic data to the global understanding of SARS‑CoV‑2 Delta variant diversity, emphasizing the critical role of regional surveillance in pandemic response and preparedness.

frontmatter.title: The Concept of Balance as an Aesthetic Value in Contemporary Sculpture
frontmatter.description: Theoretical examination of 'balance' not just as a physical necessity but as a core philosophical element in regional Kurdish sculpture.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This theoretical study examines the concept of balance as an aesthetic value in contemporary sculpture, particularly in the context of regional Kurdish artistic practice. The research explores balance not merely as a physical requirement but as a fundamental philosophical and aesthetic principle in sculpture.

## Methodology

The study employed theoretical analysis and art criticism methods to examine balance in contemporary Kurdish sculpture. Artistic works were analyzed for their use of balance as both physical structure and aesthetic value, with consideration of cultural and philosophical contexts.

## Key Findings

The analysis revealed important insights:

- **Aesthetic Principle**: Balance as a core philosophical element in sculpture beyond physical necessity
- **Cultural Context**: How balance functions within Kurdish artistic traditions
- **Philosophical Dimensions**: Theoretical exploration of balance as an aesthetic value
- **Contemporary Practice**: Examination of balance in modern Kurdish sculpture

## Implications

These findings contribute to:

- Understanding aesthetic theory in regional art practice
- Art criticism and interpretation of Kurdish sculpture
- Theoretical approaches to balance in contemporary art

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates the importance of balance as both a physical and philosophical element in contemporary Kurdish sculpture, providing valuable insights into aesthetic values and artistic practice in the region.

frontmatter.title: Role of Sex Chromatin on performance in the Arabi sheep
frontmatter.description: Conducted on 122 Arabi sheep in Erbil from July 2014 to August 2015, this study assessed how sex chromatin shapes affect milk production, fertility and other reproductive traits. The findings showed significant effects of chromatin shapes on daily milk production and reproduction; the repeatability coefficient for daily milk production was estimated at 0.42.

publications.body:
## Abstract

This longitudinal study examined 122 Arabi sheep in Erbil over a 14-month period (July 2014 to August 2015) to assess the relationship between sex chromatin morphology and productive performance, particularly milk production and reproductive traits.

## Methodology

The research monitored 122 Arabi sheep throughout the study period, documenting sex chromatin shapes and measuring productive performance indicators including daily milk production and various reproductive parameters. Statistical analysis was conducted to evaluate repeatability and heritability estimates.

## Key Findings

The study revealed significant findings regarding sex chromatin and performance:

- **Milk Production**: Sex chromatin shapes showed significant effects on daily milk production patterns
- **Reproductive Traits**: Chromatin morphology influenced multiple reproductive performance indicators
- **Repeatability**: The repeatability coefficient for daily milk production was estimated at 0.42
- **Temporal Patterns**: The longitudinal design allowed for assessment of consistency in performance across seasons

## Implications

These results have practical applications for:

- Breeding programs in Arabi sheep populations
- Predicting productive performance based on chromatin characteristics
- Understanding genetic factors influencing milk production and fertility

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates the significant role of sex chromatin morphology in determining productive and reproductive performance in Arabi sheep, with practical implications for livestock breeding and management strategies in the Kurdistan region.

frontmatter.title: Role of sex chromatin on performance in the local (black) goats
frontmatter.description: Researchers examined 132 black goats to study the influence of sex chromatin shapes (drum stick, sessile nodule, tear drop, small club) on milk production, fertility and birth weight. Sex chromatin shape significantly affected daily milk yield, fertility rate and other traits; goats with drum‑stick chromatin produced the most milk (≈681 g day⁻¹).

publications.body:
## Abstract

This comprehensive study examined 132 local black goats to investigate the relationship between sex chromatin morphology and productive performance traits. The research analyzed the influence of different sex chromatin shapes on milk production, fertility rates, and birth weight characteristics in this indigenous goat breed.

## Methodology

The study evaluated 132 black goats, documenting their sex chromatin shapes and measuring various performance indicators including daily milk yield, fertility rates, and birth weight. Statistical analysis was performed to determine correlations between chromatin morphology and productive traits.

## Key Findings

The research revealed significant associations between sex chromatin shapes and productive performance:

- **Chromatin Shapes Studied**: Drum stick, sessile nodule, tear drop, and small club morphologies
- **Milk Production**: Goats with drum‑stick chromatin produced the highest daily milk yield (≈681 g day⁻¹)
- **Fertility Impact**: Sex chromatin shape significantly affected fertility rates
- **Birth Weight**: Chromatin morphology was associated with variations in birth weight
- **Trait Relationships**: Strong correlations were observed between chromatin shape and multiple productive traits

## Implications

These findings provide valuable insights for:

- Selective breeding programs targeting specific productive traits
- Understanding genetic markers associated with performance in local goat breeds
- Improving livestock productivity through chromatin-based selection criteria

## Conclusion

The study demonstrates the important role of sex chromatin morphology as a potential marker for productive performance in local black goats, offering practical applications for livestock improvement and breeding strategies.

frontmatter.title: Fenk Amjad Hasan
frontmatter.subtitle: Researcher in Psychology and Education
frontmatter.description: Profile of Fenk Amjad Hasan, Researcher in Psychology and Education
frontmatter.bio: Fenk Amjad Hasan works at the Scientific Research Center of Salahaddin University‑Erbil. Her research interests lie in psychology and education, particularly in how parental treatment influences adolescent mental health.
frontmatter.content:
Fenk Amjad Hasan works at the Scientific Research Center of Salahaddin University‑Erbil. Her research interests lie in psychology and education, particularly in how parental treatment influences adolescent mental health.

In a field study of social phobia among secondary‑school students in Erbil, Hasan and her colleague Jalal Ahmed Abdullah surveyed 402 students and found that levels of social phobia were generally low and that parenting styles were predominantly democratic. The study concluded there were no significant differences in social phobia based on sex, educational level or type of school.

She continues to explore topics such as adolescent behavior, parental influence and social anxiety, providing data to inform mental‑health interventions in Kurdistan.

frontmatter.bio: Dr Polla Fattah is a lecturer in the Department of Software Engineering at Salahaddin University‑Erbil and an active researcher in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and data mining.
frontmatter.content:
Dr Polla Fattah is a lecturer in the Department of Software Engineering at Salahaddin University‑Erbil and an active researcher in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and data mining. On his academic CV he states that he aims to harness computation to better understand thinking and information processing and to develop algorithms for automating data extraction. His goal is to use these technologies to solve complex problems and advance his society's understanding of science.

Fattah's publications include deep‑learning approaches for age and gender estimation from skeletal radiographs and Kurdish handwritten‑character recognition, as well as research on machine‑translation evaluation metrics and domain adaptation. He teaches courses such as distributed databases, advanced programming and data mining, and has received multiple letters of appreciation for excellence in teaching and research.

frontmatter.bio: Dr Salim Omar Raoof is a Doctor of Animal Breeding and Quality Assurance Manager at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. His work focuses on improving livestock performance through selection and breeding strategies.
frontmatter.content:
Dr Salim Omar Raoof is a Doctor of Animal Breeding and Quality Assurance Manager at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. His skills and expertise include animal production, breeding and genetics, cattle breeding, animal biotechnology and ruminant nutrition.

Raoof's work focuses on improving livestock performance through selection and breeding strategies; he has published studies on milk production in goats, genetic and non‑genetic factors affecting Holstein cows, and quality management in animal production systems.

In addition to research, Raoof teaches courses in animal science and provides training to farmers and students on genetics and breeding practices. He participates in committees responsible for evaluating animal production programs and works to enhance quality assurance in university laboratories and farms. His combination of practical breeding experience and academic expertise makes him a key figure in the region's livestock industry.

frontmatter.title: Dr. Samir Jawdat Bilal
frontmatter.subtitle: Assistant Professor of Fish Parasitology
frontmatter.description: Profile of Dr. Samir Jawdat Bilal, Assistant Professor of Fish Parasitology
frontmatter.bio: Samir Jawdat Bilal is an assistant professor of fish parasitology in the College of Agriculture at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. He teaches and supervises in the biology department and his research interests centre on fish diseases and parasitology, ichthyology, ecology and fisheries science.
frontmatter.content:
Samir Jawdat Bilal is an assistant professor of fish parasitology in the College of Agriculture at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. His ResearchGate biography notes that he teaches and supervises in the biology department and that his research interests centre on fish diseases and parasitology, ichthyology, ecology and fisheries science.

He has led a project titled Review of Iraqi fish parasitic fauna, which examines parasites that affect fish in Iraqi waters, and he regularly publishes on topics such as fish biology, fisheries management and the reproductive biology of fish.

Bilal's expertise extends to fish ecology and environmental monitoring. His research list includes studies on the prevalence of various protozoan and helminth parasites in fish and on the impacts of water quality on fish health. Through these projects he contributes to improving fishery management and disease control strategies in Iraq. As an academic he also mentors graduate students and collaborates with regional fisheries organizations to address aquatic animal health issues.

frontmatter.title: Sara Abdulkhaliq Yasin
frontmatter.subtitle: Master of Science in Phycolimnology
frontmatter.description: Profile of Sara Abdulkhaliq Yasin, Researcher in Environmental Sciences
frontmatter.bio: Sara Abdulkhaliq Yasin holds a Master's degree in phycolimnology and works in the Department of Environmental Sciences at Salahaddin University‑Erbil.
frontmatter.content:
Sara Abdulkhaliq Yasin holds a Master's degree in phycolimnology and works in the Department of Environmental Sciences at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. Her ResearchGate profile lists skills in environmental science, algae and water analysis, and shows that she studies heavy‑metal exposure and oxidative stress in humans.

Recent publications evaluate the impact of heavy metals on gasoline‑station workers, linking metal exposure to cardiovascular and respiratory stress, and assess the levels of contaminants in groundwater and tap water.

Yasin also contributes to water‑quality assessments and ecological monitoring. Her work combines biomonitoring of trace metals with measurements of oxidative‑stress biomarkers in human blood, helping to identify health risks associated with environmental pollution.

frontmatter.title: Sarbast Muhsen Azeez
frontmatter.subtitle: Assistant Lecturer in Fine Arts
frontmatter.description: Profile of Sarbast Muhsen Azeez, Assistant Lecturer in Fine Arts
frontmatter.bio: Sarbast Muhsen Azeez is affiliated with the Sculpture Division of the Department of Fine Arts at Salahaddin University's Scientific Research Centre.
frontmatter.content:
Sarbast Muhsen Azeez is affiliated with the Sculpture Division of the Department of Fine Arts at Salahaddin University's Scientific Research Centre. In a 2025 article he examined the concept of balance as an aesthetic value in contemporary sculpture in the Kurdistan Region.

The study analysed types of balance—symmetrical, asymmetrical and illusory—and showed that Kurdish sculptors use balance to harmonize masses and spaces and achieve visual stability. The research concludes that balance is a fundamental aesthetic principle in contemporary Kurdish sculpture.

Azeez's interest in aesthetics and fine arts suggests he focuses on art criticism and sculpture theory, exploring how formal elements contribute to artistic meaning. As an assistant lecturer, he likely teaches sculpture and conducts research on the artistic heritage of Kurdistan. The available article underscores his effort to analyse and document contemporary art practices in the region.

frontmatter.title: Shaho Jangi Noori
frontmatter.subtitle: Researcher in Water Resource Management
frontmatter.description: Profile of Shaho Jangi Noori, Researcher in Water Resource Management
frontmatter.bio: Shaho Jangi Noori is a researcher interested in water‑resource management and rainwater harvesting.
frontmatter.content:
Shaho Jangi Noori is a researcher interested in water‑resource management and rainwater harvesting. In a review article co‑authored with Redvan Ghasemlounia, he notes that rainwater harvesting has gained renewed importance in arid and semi‑arid regions since the 1970s.

The paper highlights that selecting suitable sites using remote sensing and GIS techniques is essential for maximizing harvested water and reducing ecological impacts. It summarizes criteria from previous studies, including climate, soil, topography and land use, for assessing potential rainwater‑harvesting sites.

Noori's work emphasizes the integration of geographic information systems (GIS) and multi‑criteria decision analysis for site selection. His contributions help guide water‑resource planners and engineers in designing efficient harvesting systems, especially in regions facing water shortages.

frontmatter.title: Shakar Jamal Aweez
frontmatter.subtitle: Researcher in Environmental Science
frontmatter.description: Profile of Shakar Jamal Aweez, Researcher in Environmental Science
frontmatter.bio: Shakar Jamal Aweez is affiliated with the Scientific Research Centre at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. He specializes in environmental remediation and the application of nanotechnology to treat contaminated sites.
frontmatter.content:
Shakar Jamal Aweez is affiliated with the Scientific Research Centre at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. He participated in an environmental study that assessed heavy‑metal contamination of soils near the Khabat and Bazian oil‑refinery sites in Iraq.

The researchers found elevated concentrations of chromium, nickel and cadmium in the soil and concluded that these metals pose a serious environmental and health threat. The team tested green nanoscale zero‑valent iron (nZVI) particles and observed that they effectively reduced heavy‑metal concentrations in polluted soils.

Aweez's research interests therefore encompass soil pollution, environmental remediation and the application of nanotechnology to treat contaminated sites. His work contributes to sustainable environmental management and demonstrates how novel materials can mitigate industrial pollution.

frontmatter.bio: Suhad Asad Mustafa heads the molecular genetics laboratory at the General Directorate of Scientific Research Center at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. She holds a PhD in molecular genetics from the University of Wales (United Kingdom).
frontmatter.content:
Suhad Asad Mustafa heads the molecular genetics laboratory at the General Directorate of Scientific Research Center at Salahaddin University‑Erbil. She holds a BSc and MSc in biology from the same university and obtained a PhD in molecular genetics from the University of Wales (United Kingdom).

Mustafa's profile lists expertise in microRNA, biosensors, genotyping, enzymes, mutation analysis, cancer genomics and expression profiling.

Her research group investigates gene expression patterns and molecular markers in cancer and infectious diseases. She collaborates on projects developing biosensors for pathogen detection and leads training workshops on molecular techniques. As a keynote speaker she promotes scientific research in Kurdistan and mentors postgraduate students in genetics and biotechnology.

frontmatter.title: Treska Salih Hassan
frontmatter.subtitle: Researcher in Molecular Biology and Cancer Research
frontmatter.description: Profile of Treska Salih Hassan, Researcher in Molecular Biology and Cancer Research
frontmatter.bio: Treska Salih Hassan is a researcher from Salahaddin University‑Erbil whose work bridges molecular biology and cancer research.
frontmatter.content:
Treska Salih Hassan is a researcher from Salahaddin University‑Erbil whose work bridges molecular biology and cancer research. She co‑authored a paper showing that activation of liver X receptor (LXR) inhibits proliferation of human breast‑cancer cells by suppressing the PI3K–Akt signalling pathway.

The study reported that LXR activation reduced phosphorylation of key kinases in the pathway and induced tumour‑suppressor phosphatases such as PTEN and PHLPP. By demonstrating that LXR ligands impair breast‑cancer cell growth and tumour formation in mice, the research suggests LXR agonists as potential anti‑cancer agents.

Hassan's research interests therefore include cancer biology, molecular signalling and the development of therapeutic agents that modulate nuclear receptors. Her contributions add to the understanding of how metabolic signalling pathways can be targeted in cancer therapy.
